evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is a foundational capability and does not inherently require another story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators to a game via a URL inherently depends on a game existing to invite them to.

evaluations.evidence: start a round ... so that we can estimate it
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game/session context in which the round occurs.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items in a session depends on items being created/added for that session.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item inherently requires that items already exist in a list/session.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to a list for estimation presupposes an existing game/session context where such a list exists.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item inherently depends on items having been added/created first.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item inherently depends on items existing first.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates presupposes that estimates can be given within a round/game.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average inherently depends on estimates having been collected.

evaluations.evidence: filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling based on all estimators' cards depends on the existence of estimator participation and card/estimate submission.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate presupposes an estimation round/item context to attach the estimate to.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating inherently depends on prior estimation having occurred in the session.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories implies there is a destination list/session/game to import them into.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/pasting stories implies there is a destination list/session/game to add them to.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games inherently depends on games having been created/stored previously.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript depends on games existing and transcript data being available from them.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the ability to view/access a game transcript.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the ability to view/access a game transcript.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game inherently depends on games existing to delete.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is self-contained and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently depends on accounts existing to authenticate against.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details inherently depends on an account existing (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account inherently depends on an account existing (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a cross-cutting presentation requirement and does not inherently depend on a specific other story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders inherently depend on accounts (with stored email/password reset data) existing.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting a card/scale option presupposes an estimation game/round where cards are used.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators depends on the base invite-to-game capability and a game to invite them to.

evaluations.evidence: join a game ... on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL inherently depends on a game existing and an invitation/link being provided.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item being estimated depends on items existing and a round/item being selected for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items in the session depends on items having been created/added for that session.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This depends on estimators being able to join and submit estimates in a round.

evaluations.evidence: shown all estimates ... after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates after submission depends on the capability for estimators to participate and submit estimates.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until ... all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the existence of estimate submission and the reveal/show-estimates mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Prior estimates can only exist if estimates have been captured for stories/rounds previously.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: This depends on a current round existing and estimates being submitted within it.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer for participants presupposes a multiplayer game/session context with participants present.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself
evaluations.rationale: Resetting 'the two-minute timer' inherently depends on the timer feature existing.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds depends on rounds having occurred and their stories/estimates being stored/displayed.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering across draws presupposes the existence of draws/estimation with cards.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the ability to submit an estimate and on the concept of a draw/round lifecycle.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a participant photo near played cards depends on participants existing in a game and on the UI area where cards are played.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a general quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A glossary can be created independently of other functional stories.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing is an internal optimization task that does not inherently require another specific story to be implemented first at the requirement level.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a general quality requirement and not inherently dependent on a particular other story.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a general quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a cross-cutting quality requirement and not inherently dependent on a specific other story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a general capability/constraint and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Predictable URLs are a general design requirement and do not inherently depend on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages can be implemented as a general mechanism without requiring a particular other story first.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing 'results' presupposes that the system captures/stores estimation outcomes to begin with.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Usage metrics inherently depend on the game being used and usage events/data being generated by core gameplay features.
